            (A) in the first sentence—
                (i) by striking “The” and inserting “Notwithstanding section 201(f), the”; and

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the words "hearing" and "rule" signal a public hearing or rulemaking. But this section only makes technical and conforming amendments to the Federal Power Act: it updates cross-references, fixes grammar, and corrects typos. It does not itself create or require any hearing, comment period, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: by striking “hearing had” and inserting “hearing held”

opus.w: This section is only technical and conforming amendments to the Federal Power Act: it updates cross-referenced section numbers and fixes typos. The 'hearing had' to 'hearing held' change and the added words 'or rule' are tempting, but neither creates or requires a hearing, a comment period, a rulemaking, a consultation, or a right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. They only reword existing text, so nothing here brings outside parties into a federal decision.
opus.s: in the first sentence of subsection (a), by striking “hearing had” and inserting “hearing held”
opus.b:
I labelled this **No**.

The tempting reading is "Yes." Subsection (b)(1) mentions a hearing, since it changes "hearing had" to "hearing held" in FPA §206(a). Subsection (a)(1)(B)(i) adds the words "or rule" after "any order," which might look like rulemaking authority. Both fail against the definition. The hearing change only fixes the wording of an existing provision; it does not create or require any new hearing or outside input. Adding "or rule" widens which Commission orders or rules reach certain entities; it does not grant or require a rulemaking or a comment period. Everything else in the section renumbers cross-references or corrects typos.

I'm moderately confident (0.78). The "hearing held" change touches an existing FERC rate hearing that outside parties take part in, and "or rule" mentions rules, so a reviewer could plausibly call this "Yes."

qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: The text mentions "hearing held" and "hearing had," which are keywords associated with public participation.
Resolution: These references are merely technical amendments to existing statutory language regarding administrative procedures for the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. They do not establish a new requirement for public consultation, comment periods, or advisory boards involving outside parties in the context of this specific section's amendments. The section is purely a list of textual changes to other sections of the Federal Power Act.
